  id = {EDN-18},
  title = {Unseen countries and models are accepted with a warning},
  note = {\textbf{Absorbs EDN-42} (2026-09-30): the pipeline encodes an unseen categorical value as missing.},
  date = {2026-09-29},
  milestone = {M4: Model Deployment},
  topic = {API Design, Feature Encoding},
  participants = {@lukas2510},
  decision = {A \texttt{country\_\allowbreak{}code} or a \texttt{model} that the training data does not contain is accepted, passed to the model as unknown, and reported in the response's \texttt{warnings} field (FR-05).
The \texttt{features} stage follows the same rule: a categorical has the training levels only, and any other value becomes missing.
The \texttt{ES} holdout's \texttt{country\_\allowbreak{}code} is therefore missing in every row, on purpose.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item Reject with HTTP 422: every \texttt{ES} listing would be refused, so the drift scenario of EDN-03 could not be replayed.
\item Give the holdout country a level of its own: the model would receive a code it was never fitted on.
\item Drop \texttt{country\_\allowbreak{}code} from the features: discards a real price driver to tidy one holdout frame.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} EDN-03 holds Spain out so that unseen traffic can be replayed against the running API.
LightGBM handles a missing category natively, so nothing has to be built.
The scope check we do want is the make, which keeps its 422 (FR-04).
The \texttt{features} stage warns about a column that a split never fills, and a test pins the holdout case.},
  ai = {Alternative assessment, Recommendation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI pointed out that EDN-03 had already settled the API rule.
An adversarial AI review later found the empty holdout column on the real snapshot and recommended documenting it instead of changing the encoding.
We accepted both.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code sessions of 2026-09-29 (PR \#19) and 2026-09-30 (review of PR \#55).},
